expl.summary: Each of the 16 neurons is an intercept plus a sum of if-statements on jet observables (steps, products of two steps and a few linear terms), clipped at zero and rounded to the network's number grid; each class score adds some neurons and subtracts others, and the largest score decides. This is the one-term version of formula 250 (per neuron each observable appears in at most one term), re-tuned on the network's predictions; it classifies 80.8% of validation jets correctly. The g score rests on multiplicity (neuron 1: high ln ΣpT and −Σz ln z, many particles; +43%; freezing it costs 11.2 accuracy points, the most), which the q score subtracts (-19%). Both light-parton scores subtract neuron 4, which is off for jets lighter than 78.2 GeV and falls with D₂(β=2) and τ₂₁(β=2) (-37% of the q score, -21% of the g score), and add neuron 9, large for jets lighter than 91.0 GeV with high τ₂₁(β=2) (+26% and +16%); the g score follows N₂ (0.717), the q score D₂(β=2) (0.72). The W and Z scores both subtract neuron 8, on for jets heavier than 103 GeV with large λ₁+λ₂ (-25% and -29%), and add neuron 5, few particles with ΣpT(50 hardest) above 943 GeV (+11% and +14%). They are split by mass: neuron 0, pushed down above 82.8 GeV, raises the W score (+11%) and lowers the Z score (-22%); neuron 7, largest between 91.2 and 121 GeV, raises the Z score (+9.9%) and lowers the W score (-6.4%); neuron 14, on above 87.4 GeV, lowers the W score (-8.9%). The W score follows the jet mass (rank correlation -0.692), the Z score λ₂ (-0.593). The t score subtracts neuron 13, a ln ΣpT scale switched off for jets heavier than 163-173 GeV (-40%), and adds neuron 10 (m(harder of 2 subjets) above 65.0 GeV, large e₂; +26%); it follows τ₁ (0.75). The thresholds 91.2 GeV (neuron 7) and 172 and 173 GeV (neurons 5 and 13) match offered candidate values, the Z and top masses; the jet mass here is that of the 64 particles seen.

It is pushed up for (m/ΣpT)² < 0.00766 (+14.9%) and, partly restoring the mass step, when m(50 hardest) > 82.0 GeV (+5.3%), and pushed down for very small ΣzᵢzⱼΔRᵢⱼ² (< 0.00614, -8.7%). Smaller terms push it up for n(0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4) < 15.3 (+4.6%) and down for z(0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4) < 0.0913 (-2.6%), τ₁ < 0.0699 (-2.5%) and ΣzΔR²(20 hardest) < 0.00652 (-2.3%). Over all jets it falls with mass (rank correlation -0.661), m(50 hardest) (-0.639) and with m/ΣpT, (m/ΣpT)², λ₁+λ₂ and ΣzΔR² (-0.635 each), because the heavy jets sit at zero. W jets sit highest (1.78), then quarks (0.715), gluons (0.335) and Z jets (0.264), with tops lowest (0.103). It is zero for 1.5% of W jets, 17.7% of quarks, 46.2% of gluons, 50.8% of Z jets and 89.7% of tops.
